sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Holland different?
sections.html:
Holland straddles a county line, and that shapes almost every step of a sale. Thirty-second Street divides the city between Ottawa County on the north and Allegan County on the south, so the deed, the treasurer and the school district can all depend on which side your house stands. Whether you list it, sell it yourself or accept an as-is cash purchase, start by confirming the county for your parcel.

The city sits beside Lake Macatawa, about 5 miles east of Lake Michigan, and covers 17.45 square miles of which 9.08 are in Ottawa County and 8.13 in Allegan County. Holland is the largest city in both counties. The Census Bureau estimates 35,372 residents as of July 1, 2025, a gain of 2.9 percent over the 2020 estimates base, which makes it one of the few places in this group that is still adding people.

sections.h2: What is the Holland housing market built on?
sections.html:
Dutch Calvinist settlers led by Albertus van Raalte founded Holland in 1847, and the city incorporated in 1867. A fire on October 8 to 10, 1871 burned most of downtown, so the oldest surviving homes cluster in the Historic District and nearby streets rather than in the original core. Neighborhoods people mention include Holland Heights, Westside, Washington Square, Hope, Maplewood, South End and Downtown.

Jobs come from manufacturing, tourism, agriculture and higher education. Employers listed for the area include Herman Miller, Haworth, Adient, Magna and Kraft Heinz, and the city is home to Hope College and a Grand Valley State University campus. The Tulip Time festival each May brings visitors who book local homes, which is why the short-term rental rules below carry a special festival category.

sections.h2: How do Holland home values and ownership compare with other Michigan cities?
sections.html:
Among Holland, Kalamazoo, Hamtramck and Jackson, Holland has the highest median home value. The 2020 to 2024 Census figures give the shape of the market:

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $252,200.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 67.8 percent across 12,977 households.
  • Median gross rent: $1,193.
  • Persons per household: 2.34, and 23.6 percent of residents are Hispanic or Latino.
  • Mean commute to work: 16.8 minutes.

A short commute and an employer base that includes furniture makers and automotive suppliers keep demand for starter homes steady, but a house that needs a new roof, furnace or foundation work still sells at a discount to the median. A cash buyer pricing a repair-heavy house will start from the repaired value and subtract the work.

sections.h2: Which county offices and school district apply to my Holland house?
sections.html:
Nearly all of the Ottawa County side lies inside Holland Public Schools. On the Allegan County side, much of the city is in Holland Public Schools and the rest falls in Hamilton Community Schools. The city's own millage table reflects this split with a separate Allegan Hamilton line.

Deeds are recorded with the register of deeds in the county where the parcel sits. Ottawa County's recording office is on Fillmore Street in West Olive, and its register accepts e-recording and a consumer e-recording portal for one-time filings. Allegan County's register of deeds handles recording for the southern side. Delinquent tax questions go to the Ottawa or Allegan County Treasurer, while the current bill comes from the City of Holland Treasurer.

sections.h2: What does the Holland property tax bill look like, and when is it due?
sections.html:
The city dates the summer bill July 1 and sets the payment deadline in mid-August; the 2026 summer bill was due August 17. Winter bills go out December 1. The city adds a 1 percent administration fee to both bills. Seniors, disabled owners and other qualifying homestead taxpayers can apply to defer the summer payment; a 2026 deferral moved the due date to February 16, 2027.

sections.h2: Can a buyer or tenant use my Holland house as a rental?
sections.html:
Holland regulates rentals in Chapter 14 of its ordinance code, and the rules affect the value of an occupied rental. Every rental unit must be registered, and the registration fee is billed each year and due by December 10; failing to register or to report a change costs a $200 late fee, and not paying the annual fee is a misdemeanor violation. Each unit is inspected every 3 or 6 years before a Certificate of Compliance is awarded, and the guide for monthly or annual leases states an inspection every 3 years.

Short-term rentals follow a separate track. The city sorts them into three types:

  • Owner-occupied: the owner's primary residence, allowed in any zone district.
  • Investor-owned: the owner does not live there; allowed in mixed-use, industrial and similar districts, and in residential districts only under a cap of 25 properties with a 500-foot separation. Ask the city whether any openings exist.
  • Tulip Time: a home offered no more than 10 days during the May festival, with no inspection or certificate required.

If your buyer wants an investor-owned short-term rental in a residential zone, check capacity with the city before closing.

sections.h2: What does transfer tax cost on a Holland sale?
sections.html:
Michigan charges the seller. The state tax is $3.75 for every $500 of price (MCL 207.525), and the county tax adds 55 cents per $500 where the county has under 2,000,000 residents (MCL 207.504). On a $250,000 sale that means 500 units of $500 at $4.30 each, or $2,150. Pay the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed.

Gifts to a child or grandchild, transfers ordered by a court without a stated price, and deeds from foreclosed government-backed loans are exempt under MCL 207.526. If part of your house lies in each county, which is rare but possible near 32nd Street, ask both registers how the parcel is recorded.

sections.h2: Which Holland tax exemptions end or start when the house sells?
sections.html:
The principal residence exemption is the one that changes at closing. State law (MCL 211.7cc) tells an owner to file a rescission within 90 days after the house stops being their principal residence, and a new owner who moves in files an affidavit by June 1 to cover the summer bill or by November 1 for the winter bill. Holland's assessing office handles both forms.

The city's tax page lists other relief as well: a home repair exemption under Public Act 25 of 1978 that holds assessed value steady until the home is sold, a poverty exemption under MCL 211.7u, and a disabled veteran exemption. If you used any of them, tell the buyer, because the first bill after closing may look different.

sections.h2: How do the lake and climate affect a Holland house?
sections.html: Holland has a humid continental climate moderated by Lake Michigan. January daily highs average 31.8 degrees with lows near 19.9, and the record low of minus 24 shows that a furnace failure in the winter can freeze pipes. Summer highs average 81.7 degrees in July. Homes near Lake Macatawa and the Macatawa River sit at about 610 feet of elevation, so ask a buyer's inspector to check basements for moisture and plan any gutter or grading repairs before showings.

faqs.q: Which county do I record my Holland deed in?
faqs.a: The county where your parcel sits. Holland spans Ottawa County to the north and Allegan County to the south along 32nd Street, and each county has its own register of deeds.

faqs.q: When is the City of Holland summer tax due?
faqs.a: Mid-August. The 2026 summer bill was dated July 1 and due August 17. Winter bills are issued December 1, and the city adds a 1 percent administration fee to both.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental certificate to sell a Holland rental?
faqs.a: The registration and Certificate of Compliance belong to the rental operation, and the city asks owners to report ownership changes. Failure to register or report a change carries a $200 late fee, so tell the city about the sale.

faqs.q: Can a buyer run an Airbnb in my Holland house?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied short-term rentals are allowed in any zone. Investor-owned ones are limited in residential districts to 25 properties with 500 feet of separation, so check capacity first.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax will I owe on a Holland sale?
faqs.a: $4.30 per $500 of price in a county under 2,000,000 residents, made of $3.75 state and $0.55 county. A $200,000 sale costs $1,720. Family transfers to children and grandchildren are exempt.
